newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 17.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Chairman of New Korea Party Lee Hong-koo proposed that if the nationwide strikes are stopped and opposition parties hold dialogue, he would more actively seek a solution to the present crisis, such as recommending top political talks.

- The opposition United Liberal Democratic Party and National Congress for New Politics announced they will pursue talks with the ruling party only when a decision is made to review the new labour and national security laws, party heads talks are held, and police action against striking unionists stopped.
- A district court decided to ask the Constitutional Court to review the constitutionality of the New Korea Party's passage of new labour laws at the end of last year.
- The government has decided to take measures for employees to receive medical insurance, various loan benefits, and tuition support for one year after being dismissed from employment.
